albums.blurb: Surprise Chef are a Melbourne outfit who record moody, entirely instrumental soul-funk in the lineage of David Axelrod and the CTI catalogue, all vintage keys, clipped drums and reverb-heavy guitar. Daylight Savings is their second album, cut in the band's home studio with engineer Henry Jenkins and released in October 2020 on Mr Bongo with their own College of Knowledge imprint; they have since signed to New York's Big Crown Records, home of the stylistically kindred El Michels Affair.
albums.reception: NME's review called it "an album teeming with movie magic," and Presto Music selected it as a Recording of the Week.

albums.blurb: Webster's third album and her first for Secretly Canadian, made at 21, is where her signature sound locked into place: languid songs that run pedal steel through Atlanta R&B, with a rap verse from Father of Awful Records — the hip-hop collective she photographed professionally — sitting naturally beside saxophone and lap steel. "Room Temperature" and "Kingston" from this record became her breakout songs.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 81 out of 100 from fifteen critics, with Pitchfork rating it 7.8 and Consequence of Sound grading it A−.

albums.blurb: Pentangle joined two of the great British acoustic guitarists, Bert Jansch and John Renbourn, with Jacqui McShee's clear-toned singing and the jazz rhythm section of Danny Thompson (double bass) and Terry Cox (drums). Basket of Light, their third album for Transatlantic, is the group's high-water mark: traditional ballads like "Once I Had a Sweetheart" set against originals such as "Light Flight," the theme to the BBC drama Take Three Girls, with the interplay swinging more than folk of the era usually dared.
albums.reception: It became the band's commercial peak, reaching No. 5 on the UK Albums Chart, and is included in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
